title: Mobility Computation Lab — Complete project structure
subtitle: Data and models · computational methods · reusable tools · three city cases
kind: conceptual module map of documented public components; not a universal executable pipeline

nodes.label: Roads · boundaries · zones
nodes.description: Published spatial inputs are prepared with source and geometry scope retained.
nodes.scope: source-dependent; not every city uses the same layers

nodes.label: Population · households · activity
nodes.description: Statistical geography, household fields, buildings or land-use activity attributes/proxies.
nodes.scope: Boston and Hong Kong have distinct bounded preparations; not Sioux Falls

nodes.label: GTFS · fares · walking access
nodes.description: Service, fare and access evidence supplies supported cost or choice attributes where documented.
nodes.scope: case-specific service snapshots and engineering assumptions

nodes.label: GPS · detectors · trajectories
nodes.description: Observation and service records require QC and explicit network association; they are not automatically OD or calibration data.
nodes.scope: observations differ by city and access rights

nodes.label: GMNS and representation layer
nodes.description: Directed physical nodes/links, fine/parent zones, centroids and nonphysical access, source IDs, units, crosswalks and provenance; turn-aware routing states are case-specific mappings.
nodes.scope: core GMNS vocabulary plus documented project extensions; transit and observations are not all core GMNS
display_lines: Directed nodes + physical links  ·  fine + parent zones
Centroids + nonphysical access  ·  IDs + units + provenance

nodes.label: Population / household / activity preparation
nodes.description: Versioned source geography and fields are allocated to zonal population, household and separate activity attributes before optional demand modeling.
nodes.scope: case-specific, not a universal city compiler

nodes.label: Four-stage demand and static assignment route
nodes.description: Stage 01 productions/attractions; 02 directed person OD; 03 mode demand and declared vehicle/PCE demand; 04 static road assignment under a declared period and objective.
nodes.scope: Boston limited and Hong Kong engineering-scenario branches; Sioux benchmark bypasses stages 01–03

nodes.label: Observation QC and matching / association
nodes.description: Positions/timestamps and service records can be linked to physical roads or service and supply supported travel-cost/parameter inputs or result queries, but do not imply observed OD.
nodes.scope: exploratory feedback is optional and case-specific

nodes.label: Already-declared OD inputs
nodes.description: Supplied vehicle OD bypasses population preparation and stages 01–03.
nodes.scope: supported direct-vehicle static entry; finite cases have separate demand preparation

nodes.label: Network + demand preparation
nodes.description: Explicit network, demand, time/period, units, access and cost contracts feed separate static and finite mathematical instances.
nodes.scope: common concepts, not one universal runner

nodes.label: Static traffic assignment
nodes.description: Fixed-demand BPR/Beckmann branch: FW, origin-based Algorithm B, finite-path controls and native Diagnostic L3/compression with original-space reconstruction.
nodes.scope: method/city adapter and numerical acceptance vary by case

nodes.label: Finite time-expanded optimization
nodes.description: Case-specific bounded time-indexed demand and graph; movement, waiting, source/sink and applicable turn/zone connectors; fixed arc costs with shared hard capacities; arc-flow LP, two-phase CG, Lagrangian and ADMM.
nodes.scope: separately versioned bounded case instances; not automatic calibrated DTA

nodes.label: Outputs, analysis and independent checks
nodes.description: Zonal/model demand; generated columns and physical-link movement/assignment flows; original-space reconstruction; saved SQLite/CSV queries; convergence/geographic views; model-specific independent evaluators and reproduction records.
nodes.scope: checks have method-specific meanings, not one universal optimality certificate
display_lines: Zonal demand · path columns · physical-link flow · reconstruction
CSV / SQLite · convergence / maps · model-specific evaluators

nodes.label: Boston
nodes.description: City-data/demand workflow, scalable static assignment and bounded finite-network studies.
nodes.scope: real-city sources with distinct static and ten-demand finite cases

nodes.label: Sioux Falls
nodes.description: Controlled static benchmark and selected-OD finite-network experiments.
nodes.scope: supplied benchmark OD, not a demographic city compiler

nodes.label: Hong Kong
nodes.description: Turn-aware bounded real-city engineering scenario with separate static and finite computational evidence.
nodes.scope: not all methods have accepted city results

nodes.label: Open-data support
nodes.description: Catalog/explorer and user-supplied data-processing tools; catalog records are not automatically ingested model inputs.
nodes.scope: source evidence, not citywide model inputs

nodes.label: Retained generic engine
nodes.description: The generic 0.3.0-rc5 network runner is distinct from later separately versioned case implementations.
nodes.scope: 0.3.0-rc5 generic engine only

nodes.label: Method implementations
nodes.description: Static and distributed method source lives under algorithms; some accepted case-specific sources remain in versioned evidence bundles.
nodes.scope: versioned method/case routes, not one CLI

nodes.label: Cases and examples
nodes.description: Examples, case pages and versioned evidence record runnable and inspectable scopes.
nodes.scope: three distinct city roles

nodes.label: Verification and presentation
nodes.description: Repository tests, saved-result checks, launcher and deterministic page/figure builders.
nodes.scope: documentation builds never run scientific solvers

nodes.label: Public navigation
nodes.description: Methods, capability tables, contributions, complete walkthrough and getting-started guide are direct public reading routes.
nodes.scope: navigation is not executable model flow
